chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The perfume in the moustache is from the character/mannerisms of the Prophets (peace be upon them) and a prestige/honor for the scribes (Recording Angels).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of applying perfume to the moustache in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the practice of applying perfume to the moustache with the noble character (akhlaq) of the Prophets, highlighting its spiritual elegance. This act is further elevated as a form of honor (karamah) for the Recording Angels (al-Katibin), suggesting that personal grooming and pleasant scent enhance one's spiritual presence and are pleasing to the celestial recorders of deeds.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The perfume in the moustache is from the mannerisms of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and a prestige for the two scribes (Recording Angels)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isa from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Applying perfume to one’s mustache is of the discipline of the Prophets ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and honoring the scribes (the angels on one’s shoulders).”’
